verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Muse has its own computer with a file system and terminal, so it can write and run its own code. They also say it can build trackers and dashboards from your data, and that everything it generates is stored in your VM, where you can inspect and download it. Chart output and computed answers are only implied by the dashboard examples, and there is no hands-on or independent corroboration of data-analysis workflows. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of chart/visualization generation, explicit computed-answer analysis over uploaded data, and independent hands-on evidence of code execution on user files.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can have the assistant write and run code on my data to produce charts, computed answers, and downloadable files

citations.quote: Muse has its own computer, with a file system and a terminal, so it can write its own code and build the tools a task needs.
It can build a tracker for your spending, an interactive study guide, or a dashboard to find patterns in your sleep.
You can inspect, edit and download these files freely
